name: odin
display_name: ODIN (28 nm FDSOI, Frenkel 2019 — measured silicon @ 0.55 V / 75 MHz)

validity.array_size_assumed: one 256-neuron, 64k-synapse crossbar core; 4-bit synapses (3-bit weight + 1 mapping bit); 320 um x 270 um
validity.notes: Measured on silicon, averaged over 9 test chips at 24 C (Fig. 8b). The declared corner is 0.55 V at f_clk = 75 MHz, the maximum frequency at that supply. ODIN's published power model is P = P_leak + P_idle x f_clk + E_SOP x r_SOP (Eq. 2), so the clock-proportional idle term is folded into p_static_per_core AT THE DECLARED CLOCK; a run at another clock must restate it and say so.

area_per_core_total.citation: frenkel2019odin Fig. 8a caption and Fig. 8b, p.8
area_per_core_total.note: 'Chip area outside the 320um x 270um of the ODIN neuromorphic processor is occupied [by other blocks]' — 320 x 270 = 86400 um^2 = 0.086 mm^2, the headline area. Supersedes the decomposed area constants; never sum both.

area_per_cell.citation: frenkel2019odin Abstract and Section III, p.1 and p.5
area_per_cell.note: 'only 0.68um2 per 4-bit synapse'. Declared for decomposition studies, not summed with the aggregate above. Cross-check: 65536 x 0.68 = 44564 um^2, i.e. 51.6% of the 86400 um^2 core — about half the core is the synapse array, leaving the neurons, the SDSP update logic, the scheduler and the controller.

area_global_fixed.derivation: The published 320 um x 270 um IS the whole neuromorphic processor and is already charged by area_per_core_total over the single core. Silicon outside it belongs to other blocks on the shared test chip, not to ODIN.

e_mac.citation: frenkel2019odin Fig. 8b and Section IV-A, p.8
e_mac.note: 'Incr. energy/SOP (ESOP) 8.43pJ @0.55V'. The INCREMENTAL energy of one more synaptic operation, measured by saturating the scheduler and subtracting leakage and idle power. The paper states it 'includes the contributions of reading and updating the synaptic weight according to the SDSP learning rule, reading and updating the associated neuron state, as well as the controller and scheduler overheads' — which is exactly why e_neuron_update is NOT declared for this target: it is already inside this number. Deliberately NOT the 12.7 pJ headline, which is Eq. (3)'s whole-chip power divided by the SOP rate and therefore contains leakage and idle power (see odin.md).

p_static_global.citation: frenkel2019odin Fig. 8b and Section IV-A, p.8
p_static_global.note: 'Leakage power (Pleak) 27.3uW @0.55V' — the P_leak term of Eq. (2), leakage with no clock activity, independent of frequency.

p_static_per_core.citation: frenkel2019odin Fig. 8b and Section IV-A, p.8
p_static_per_core.derivation: The P_idle x f_clk term of Eq. (2) evaluated at this profile's declared clock: 1.78 uW/MHz x 75 MHz = 133.5 uW. ODIN has exactly one core, so a per-core declaration charges it once.
p_static_per_core.note: Clock-proportional idle power, not leakage — a run at another clock must restate it, and 'Idle power (Pidle) 1.78uW/MHz @0.55V' is the rate to restate it from.

e_program_per_byte.citation: frenkel2019odin Fig. 8b and Section IV-A, p.8 (the e_mac anchor); Section II-B (4-bit synapse)
e_program_per_byte.derivation: [TS6] The paper reports no weight-load energy, so the commit energy is anchored on this profile's own access-scale constant. An ODIN synapse is 4 bits (3-bit weight + 1 mapping bit, conductance_levels = 8), so a byte of synaptic SRAM holds two synapses and the per-byte access anchor is 2 x e_mac = 2 x 8.43 = 16.86 pJ/B. An SRAM write costs about 1-3x its read, so the ratio band is [0.5x, 3x] the anchor = 8.43 - 50.58 pJ/B, with the nominal at the band's log-space centre, sqrt(8.43 x 50.58) = 20.6492 pJ/B.
e_program_per_byte.note: e_mac here is the INCREMENTAL energy per SOP, which the paper states already contains the weight read AND update, the neuron state read and update, and the controller and scheduler overheads - so it overstates the bare SRAM access, which is why the ratio band reaches down to 0.5x. DERIVED, not measured.

t_program_per_byte.derivation: [TS6] ODIN publishes no configuration-interface rate (its SPI bus width and clock are not stated per byte), so the wall is DONOR-SCALED from the two profiles that declare one, along validity.technology_node_nm: truenorth 800 ns/B at 28 nm stays 800 ns/B at ODIN's own 28 nm, and generic_estimated_22nm 4 / 80 / 1000 ns/B at 22 nm becomes 5.09091 / 101.818 / 1272.73 ns/B. The band is the ENVELOPE of both scaled donors, 5.09091 - 1272.73 ns/B, and the nominal is the geometric mean of their scaled nominals, sqrt(800 x 101.818) = 285.402 ns/B.
t_program_per_byte.note: Two orders of magnitude wide because the two donors disagree by that much - a scan chain against a parallel bus. Only the amortized latency_programming_s term reads it.

e_core_program.citation: frenkel2019odin Fig. 8b, p.8 (the e_mac anchor); Section II, p.2 (256 neurons)
e_core_program.derivation: [TS6] ODIN declares no e_core_init, so the payload-independent part of a program load is anchored on the core-state SWEEP this profile's own geometry defines: 256 neurons in the core (validity.array_size_assumed) x e_mac 8.43 pJ = 2.15808 nJ of per-core control work, the same compartment-sweep anchor loihi's measured e_core_init sits about 1.7x below. The ratio band [0.5x, 2x] gives 1.07904 - 4.31616 nJ, with the nominal at the band's log-space centre, 2.15808 nJ.
e_core_program.note: Charged per program LOAD (x reprogrammed_cores). ODIN is a SINGLE core, so this term is paid at most once per load on this target.

t_cycle.citation: frenkel2019odin Section II and Section IV-A, p.3 and p.8
t_cycle.derivation: 'the maximum SOP rate ODIN can handle is equal to fclk/2 as each SOP takes two clock cycles to complete' — 2 / 75 MHz = 26.667 ns per synaptic operation at the declared clock.
t_cycle.note: ODIN's pipeline step IS one SOP; there is no separate network timestep at this level.

conductance_levels.note: 'each synapse consisting of a 3-bit weight and one bit of mapping table' — 2^3 = 8 weight values. Digital SRAM synapses, so this is a precision fact, not an analog conductance count.

write_sigma.derivation: Synaptic weights live in digital SRAM, so a written weight has no analog programming spread. Zero is a fact about the technology, not a missing measurement.

read_sigma.derivation: Digital SRAM read; no analog column-current sensing, so no read spread.

area_per_adc.derivation: ODIN is an all-digital design with a time-multiplexed SRAM crossbar; there is no analog-to-digital converter in the datapath, so the count is zero by construction rather than unknown.

e_adc_conversion.derivation: No ADC exists in ODIN; see area_per_adc.

t_adc_conversion.derivation: No ADC exists in ODIN; see area_per_adc.
